scams.name: Tianfu Airport (TFU) & Chengdu Shuangliu (CTU) Taxi Scams
scams.description: Chengdu has two airports: Tianfu (TFU, the newer main one, 50 km from city center) and Shuangliu (CTU, 16 km from center, closer but serving limited flights). The legitimate metered taxi fares: TFU to Chunxi Road is ¥180–¥220 (60 min), CTU to Chunxi Road is ¥80–¥110 (30 min). A community PSA is blunt: 'Don't go with the guys waving at you at arrivals and asking if you need a taxi, scam city. Just grab one from the official rank' — the 'guys waving' are the unauthorised touts inside the terminal who quote ¥500–¥800 fixed prices. Cross-China community reports call these 'scams and trying to overcharge you. It's unbearable' and confirm the universal rule applies at every major Chinese airport. The Tianfu to CTU transfer itself is a scam vector per Chengdu locals — unlicensed drivers quote ¥200+ for what should be ¥100–¥150 on the meter. DiDi operates on both airports with app-regulated fares; the TFU DiDi pickup zone is on the arrival-level road, and CTU's is at the official rideshare area. For older travelers arriving at TFU, the practical options: (1) Metro Line 18 runs from TFU to central Chengdu (Tianfu Square station) for ¥9 in 47 minutes — scam-proof and accessible; (2) DiDi at the official pickup zone (~¥150–¥200 fare); (3) if a licensed taxi, 'da biao' and expect ¥180–¥220. At CTU, Metro Line 10 serves the airport at ¥6 (25 min to Taipingyuan) and connects to all city lines. NEVER accept a driver who approaches inside either terminal — all are unauthorised. Community reports warn that drivers offering 'cheap panda base transfer' from airports are routinely in the same scam ecosystem.
scams.avoidance: Metro Line 18 from TFU to Tianfu Square: ¥9, 47 min, scam-proof Metro Line 10 from CTU to Taipingyuan: ¥6, 25 min DiDi at official rideshare pickup zone; app-regulated fare If licensed taxi, 'da biao' (打表); expect ¥180–¥220 TFU-center, ¥80–¥110 CTU-center NEVER accept drivers approaching inside terminal — all are unauthorised
scams.location: Tianfu International Airport (TFU) arrivals, Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport (CTU), airport-to-panda-base transfers

scams.name: Chengdu Tibet Tour Permit & Package Scam
scams.description: Chengdu is the main gateway city for foreign travelers heading to Tibet (all foreigners require a Tibet Travel Permit obtained via a licensed tour operator — you cannot travel to Tibet independently). Community reports document a specific 2025 Tibet tour scam where the operator sold a 'tour to Tibet' for ¥600–¥800 when the legitimate tour price is ¥6,000–¥12,000 per person — the customer arrived in Chengdu to find the 'tour' did not actually include Tibet access and the operator had disappeared with the deposit. Community threads also document the secondary layer: legitimate Tibet tours bundled with 'Chengdu city tours' that are 80% shopping stops at jade/TCM/tea venues before Tibet departure. The scam operates at several price tiers: (1) outright fraud where no permit is obtained and the tourist is left stranded; (2) 'bait-and-switch' where the tour goes to Tibet but spends half the time at commission-paying shops; (3) 'downgrade' where a paid 'Everest Base Camp' itinerary is swapped for a Lhasa-only three-day trip. For older travelers considering a Chengdu + Tibet trip, the protective playbook: (1) book ONLY through Tibet Travel Permit-licensed operators with verifiable credentials — Tibet Vista (tibettravel.org), Explore Tibet, Great Tibet Tour, Budget Tibet Tour are community-vetted; (2) pay via credit card for chargeback leverage — never Bizum, bank transfer, or cash deposits; (3) verify the permit number on your Tibet Travel Permit before traveling — permit validation via the Tibet Tourism Bureau's website is possible; (4) confirm written itinerary with ZERO shopping stops and specific site visits named; (5) expect ¥6,000–¥12,000 per person for a 4–8 day Tibet tour (Lhasa + Namtso Lake or Lhasa + Yarlung Valley) — anything under ¥3,000 is likely to end badly.
scams.avoidance: Book only with Tibet Travel Permit-licensed operators: Tibet Vista, Explore Tibet, Great Tibet Tour Pay via credit card; never Bizum, Alipay, or bank transfer Verify permit number on Tibet Tourism Bureau website before traveling Confirm written itinerary with ZERO shopping stops and specific named sites Expect ¥6,000–¥12,000 per person for 4–8 day Lhasa tour; reject lower prices
scams.location: Chengdu hotels, Chengdu North Railway Station booths, online travel sites marketing 'Chengdu + Tibet' packages

scams.name: Chengdu Panda Base Tour Package Overcharge
scams.description: The Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding (Xiongmao Jidi) is the city's must-visit attraction and the scam economy around it mirrors the Great Wall ecosystem in Beijing. Hotel concierges and street touts sell 'panda base tour' packages at ¥300–¥500 per person when the actual cost is: ¥55 entry + ¥15 metro/bus + ¥20 taxi = ¥90 per person independently. Community reports confirm the self-guided option and warn about hotel-booking markups. Community threads also cover the multiple-venue confusion that scammers exploit — there are actually three main panda facilities near Chengdu (Chengdu Research Base, Dujiangyan, Wolong) and bundled tours sometimes swap the advertised location. The scam variants: (1) hotel concierge sells a ¥400 'Chengdu Panda Base VIP tour' that includes standard entry + 'exclusive' photo opportunity with pandas (actually a ¥1,000 add-on not available to tourists) + transport (¥40 worth); (2) street touts near the panda base entrance sell 'skip-the-line' tickets that are actually standard-entry tickets marked up; (3) 'bundled' tours claim to visit Chengdu Research Base but actually drive to the cheaper Bifengxia or Ya'an venues 90+ minutes out of the city. For older travelers, the clean route: (1) book Panda Base entry (¥55 adult) directly via the official WeChat mini-program '成都大熊猫繁育研究基地' or Trip.com/Ctrip; (2) take Metro Line 3 to Panda Avenue Station (Panda Dadao, ¥4) then walk or catch shuttle bus #16; (3) for a guided experience, book a licensed small-group tour on Viator or GetYourGuide (¥200–¥300 per person including transport and guide); (4) the best viewing time is 8:30–10:00 AM when pandas are most active — arrive before 8:30 via early Metro to beat the tour-group crowds; (5) for a 'photo with panda' experience, it is NOT available to foreign tourists at the Chengdu Research Base — any concierge claiming otherwise is misrepresenting.
scams.avoidance: Book Panda Base entry (¥55 adult) via official WeChat 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地 or Trip.com Metro Line 3 to Panda Avenue Station (¥4), then shuttle #16 to park entrance Arrive before 8:30 AM for best panda activity and fewer tour groups For guide, use Viator or GetYourGuide (¥200–¥300) — no shopping stops Do NOT trust any 'photo with panda' offer — not available to adult foreign tourists
scams.location: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, Dujiangyan Panda Base, Wolong Panda Base, hotel-concierge tour packages

scams.name: Chengdu Tea House Scam at Kuanzhai Alley & Jinli
scams.description: Chengdu's tourist tea-house scene at Kuanzhai Alley and Jinli Street has been infiltrated by the same scam network operating in Beijing and Shanghai, though the Chengdu variant is gentler and sometimes ambiguous. The script: a fluent-English stranger at Kuanzhai Alley or Jinli invites the tourist to a 'traditional Sichuan tea ceremony' at a side-street venue. The bill is typically ¥800–¥2,500 per person — less extreme than Beijing/Shanghai's ¥3,000–¥8,000 versions but still 10–20x the residential tea-house rate. A 2025 traveler documented the Chengdu variant: 'the general consensus is that this was very likely some kind of scam, and even if it wasn't, the risk of engaging is high enough to always walk away.' Community travel manuals document the genuine alternative: People's Park Heming Tea Garden (a 1923 institution with posted prices ¥15–¥30 per pot, bottomless refills, and no solicitation) is the authentic Chengdu tea experience that foreign tourists should seek. Wenshu Monastery's tea garden is another community-verified venue. Community reports warn 2025 first-timers about strangers approaching in tourist zones. For older travelers visiting Chengdu's old-city areas, the rule matches Beijing/Shanghai: walk past ANY stranger approaching in fluent English with a tea or cultural invitation. Do not take photos for strangers who then strike up conversation. For genuine Sichuan tea culture, go directly to People's Park Heming Tea Garden (Renmin Park, west entrance, ¥15–¥30 per pot) or Wenshu Monastery's tea garden (¥20–¥40 per pot). Both have posted prices and serve locals daily.
scams.avoidance: Walk past any stranger approaching at Kuanzhai Alley, Jinli, or People's Park with 'bu yao xie xie' For genuine tea: People's Park Heming Tea Garden (¥15–¥30 per pot, bottomless) Alternative: Wenshu Monastery tea garden (¥20–¥40 per pot) Never follow a stranger to a side-street tea house Pay with credit card for chargeback leverage if trapped
scams.location: Kuanzhai Xiangzi (Wide and Narrow Alley) tourist strip, Jinli Ancient Street, People's Park tea-garden entrances

scams.name: Sichuan Hotpot Tourist-Menu & 'Famous Restaurant' Overcharge
scams.description: Sichuan hotpot is Chengdu's signature food experience, and the city is full of honest ¥80–¥150 per-person hotpot venues. The tourist-trap parallel: laminated-English-menu hotpot restaurants near Kuanzhai Alley, Jinli Street, and the Tianfu Square tourist corridor charge ¥300–¥500 per person for the same experience, with 'premium' side dishes at ¥80 per plate and 'traditional' oils/sauces at ¥50. The broth flavor is often reduced from what residents expect. Community threads frame genuine-venue recommendations, with 2025 community travel manuals recommending specific residential venues over Kuanzhai/Jinli tourist-strip alternatives. Community-verified authentic Chengdu hotpot venues: (1) Shu Jiu Xiang (multiple locations, the local favorite, ¥90–¥130 per person); (2) Huang Cheng Lao Ma (Kuanzhai area but institutional-quality, ¥120–¥180); (3) Da Long Yi (high-quality mid-tier, ¥130–¥170); (4) Xiao Long Kan (nationwide chain with consistent quality, ¥100–¥140). For higher-end experiences where ¥250+ per person is justified, Pu Cong Bei and Da Miao are community-respected. All have WeChat mini-program booking and published pricing. Community threads from diaspora communities cross-reference the observation that even diaspora Chinese avoid the tourist-strip venues. For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) walk one street off Kuanzhai Alley or Jinli to find honest hotpot; (2) book via WeChat mini-program (Dianping app is the Chinese Yelp — browse by rating, 4.5+ is reliable); (3) expect ¥90–¥170 per person at authentic venues; (4) NEVER follow a tout's 'famous hotpot' recommendation; (5) for the spiciest authentic experience, order Shu Jiu Xiang with yuanyang (half-spicy half-mild) broth and ask for 'yi dian dian la' (slightly spicy) if Sichuan heat is new to you.
scams.avoidance: Walk one street off Kuanzhai Alley or Jinli for honest hotpot Community names: Shu Jiu Xiang (¥90–¥130), Huang Cheng Lao Ma (¥120–¥180), Da Long Yi (¥130–¥170) Book via Dianping app (Chinese Yelp); 4.5+ ratings are reliable Expect ¥90–¥170 per person at genuine venues NEVER follow a tout's 'famous hotpot' recommendation
scams.location: Kuanzhai Alley hotpot rows, Jinli Ancient Street hotpot venues, tourist-facing Haolaihui and near Tianfu Square

scams.name: Chengdu Jade, TCM & Silk 'Museum' Shopping Tours
scams.description: Chengdu is ground zero for the 'government museum' shopping-tour scam that operates across China. Canonical community reports call Chengdu out specifically: 'We were promised a Chengdu tour in the itinerary, but ended up getting 4 scam spots in 2 days' — two full days of forced shopping stops at jade, TCM, silk, and tea 'museums' with no more than 20% of the itinerary delivered as advertised. The Chengdu variants cover: (1) Chengdu + Mount Emei / Leshan day-trips where the 4-hour bus ride each way is punctuated by 45-min shopping stops; (2) Chengdu + Jiuzhaigou 4-day packages where 30% of the trip is shopping; (3) Chengdu + Tibet bundles combining two scam layers (see dedicated Tibet scam entry). A 2025 community PSA notes: 'They carried on going on these tours when we left home and got properly scammed one time with a bait and switch' — the scam operates on older travelers specifically because tour-group dependence shields the operator from independent-traveler scrutiny. For older travelers, the protective playbook for ALL Chengdu day-trips (Mount Emei, Leshan, Dujiangyan, Jiuzhaigou): (1) book only licensed small-group tours via Viator, GetYourGuide, Tiqets, or hotel-partner Ctrip with VERIFIED 'ZERO shopping stops' in writing; (2) expect ¥300–¥800 per person for day-trip tours — anything under ¥200 includes shopping; (3) for multi-day Jiuzhaigou tours, expect ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person genuine versus ¥800–¥1,500 scam versions; (4) independent option: Chengdu's high-speed rail network makes Mount Emei (1.5 hrs, ¥65 one-way), Leshan (1 hr, ¥55), and Dujiangyan (30 min, ¥15) all easy self-guided day trips at a fraction of tour costs; (5) for Jiuzhaigou, fly to Jiuzhaigou Huanglong Airport (1 hr flight) and self-guide with a hotel driver.
scams.avoidance: Book only licensed operators with VERIFIED ZERO shopping stops in writing Expect ¥300–¥800 per person day trips; ¥2,500–¥4,000 multi-day Jiuzhaigou Self-guide via Chengdu high-speed rail: Mount Emei (¥65), Leshan (¥55), Dujiangyan (¥15) Fly direct to Jiuzhaigou Huanglong Airport for multi-day option Report shopping-stop tours to 12315 (English consumer line) for chargeback
scams.location: Tour bus stops along panda-base, Dujiangyan, Mount Emei, and Jiuzhaigou day-trip routes from Chengdu; hotel-concierge 'cultural tour' packages

scams.name: Jinli Ancient Street & Kuanzhai Alley Souvenir Overcharge
scams.description: Chengdu's tourist shopping strips — Jinli Ancient Street and Kuanzhai Alley — sell souvenirs at 2–5x residential rates. Common items: Sichuan opera mask-change 'bian lian' replicas (¥80–¥200 vs ¥20–¥50 at the city's Tongji Road souvenir market), 'handmade' silk scrolls (¥150–¥400 vs ¥40–¥100 at Qingyang Taoist temple market), Shu embroidery (¥200–¥800 vs ¥80–¥200 at dedicated craft markets). The overcharging is legal but opaque for first-time visitors. Community travel manuals recommend Tongji Road or Qingyang Market for honest pricing. The related pattern is bundled 'tea + souvenir' shopping where a pleasant-seeming stall at Jinli or Kuanzhai offers tea tasting and presents souvenirs during the tasting; the 'free' tea is really a social-obligation pressure to buy overpriced items. Community travel manuals document the view: genuine craft markets exist in Chengdu, but not on the tourist strips. For older travelers who want Sichuan-themed souvenirs, the community-recommended alternatives: (1) Tongji Road Souvenir Market (dedicated Chengdu-craft wholesale strip, 2–3x cheaper than Jinli); (2) Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market (authentic bian lian masks ¥20–¥60); (3) Shu Brocade & Embroidery Museum gift shop (official venue with certified pricing); (4) Wenshu Monastery stalls (posted prices, authentic items); (5) for Sichuan pepper and spices, any residential supermarket is 30–50% cheaper than Jinli. If shopping at Jinli/Kuanzhai for convenience, negotiate aggressively — start at 30% of first-quoted price.
scams.avoidance: Shop at Tongji Road Souvenir Market for 2–3x cheaper pricing Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market for authentic bian lian masks (¥20–¥60) Shu Brocade & Embroidery Museum gift shop for certified products If shopping Jinli/Kuanzhai for convenience, start negotiations at 30% of first-quote Decline 'free tea tasting' — it is always the setup for pressure sales
scams.location: Jinli Ancient Street (inside Wuhou Shrine area), Kuanzhai Xiangzi (Wide and Narrow Alley), People's Park handicraft vendors
